attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He names the researchers but makes the claim about their warnings himself.

semantics.note: Treating this as a checkable historical claim that these people issued warnings for years is faithful. Leaving the rhetorical question out of the assessment is correct.

contract.note: Reading 'this' as the family of harms in the previous paragraph (bias, unreliability, opacity, surveillance) is an ordinary, fair reading. So is taking 'for years' as warnings at least two years before the post. The result does depend on that broad scope, for example for Zuboff.

evidence.note: Gender Shades (2018) by Buolamwini and Gebru documents bias in commercial facial analysis, five years before the post.
Model Cards (Oct 2018) by Mitchell, Raji, Gebru and six other authors calls for transparent reporting of performance across demographic groups. The co-authors help show 'many others'.
Birhane and Prabhu's June 2020 paper warns about harmful dataset practices, more than three years before the post.
Sweeney's 2013 paper documents racial discrimination in automated ad delivery.
Zuboff's May 2019 parliamentary testimony warns about machine-driven surveillance harms. This counts under the broad surveillance reading.
Whittaker's June 2019 congressional testimony discusses bias, false facial matches and AI used for monitoring. Only the hosting path is later than 2019.

reviews.rationale: Each of the eight named people has dated public work warning about AI bias, unreliability, opacity or surveillance harms, from 2013 to 2020. All of it is at least three years before August 2023, and other co-authors add to a broader body of warnings. The packet contains no counterevidence. Under the contract's fair, broad reading of 'this', the claim is supported.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'apparently' and 'almost certainly'. 'Almost certainly' is high confidence, not a medium or low hedge, so the claim can be scored as a confident observation about the present. 'To surveil its citizens' goes slightly beyond the source, since the tools monitor travelers, who may include citizens.

contract.note: Identifying the tools as CBP's Fivecast ONYX via the linked reporting is reasonable. So is reading 'regularly' as recurring false flags in normal operation, and using August 2023 as the period.

evidence.note: 404 Media (Aug 24, 2023) confirms CBP deployed Fivecast ONYX and raises accuracy concerns, but documents no false alerts and nothing about how often they occur.

A DHS disclosure from Dec 2024, a later period, says the tools aggregate search results for human review and that ONYX was dropped for budget reasons. It says nothing about error rates in August 2023.

reviews.rationale: The evidence confirms the deployment but contains no operational records, audits or documented cases of recurring false alerts from these tools in the target period. Nothing shows they were reliable either. General evidence about AI error cannot answer the question for this specific deployment. The available evidence does not settle the claim.
